```{r}
library(tidyverse)

gapminder <- read_csv(file.path("data", "gapminder.csv"))
```

# 1. JavaScript Graphics (A): Packages

### `ggplotly()`

```{r}
plot <- gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2007) %>%
  ggplot(
    aes(
      x = gdpPercap,
      y = lifeExp,
      size = pop,
      color = continent,
      label = country
    )
  ) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.7) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = scales::label_dollar()) +
  scale_size_area(guide = "none", max_size = 15) +
  theme_bw(base_size = 14) +
  labs(
    x = "GDP per capita (log scale)",
    y = "Life expectancy (years)",
    color = "Continent"
  )

# Show only the variables that matter in the tooltip
ggplotly(plot, tooltip = c("label", "x", "y"))
```

### `reactable()`

```{r}
gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2007) %>%
  reactable(
    searchable = TRUE,
    highlight = TRUE,
    filterable = TRUE,
    defaultPageSize = 5,
    showPageSizeOptions = TRUE,
    pageSizeOptions = c(5, 10, 15)
  )
```

# 2. JavaScript Graphics (B): D3 + Claude

One possible result: the static chart above, brought to life as an animated D3 chart with a year slider, a play button, and continent filters. The code (including the data) is in `d3/gapminder-slider.html`.

<iframe src="d3/gapminder-slider.html" width="100%" height="650" style="border:none;"></iframe>

To verify it against the data, set the slider to 2007 and compare a bubble to the data:

```{r}
gapminder %>%
  filter(country == "China", year == 2007)

gapminder %>%
  filter(year == 2007) %>%
  nrow()
```
